checks: The accepted monotone, right-continuous slope g is E'_+ and approaches b. Local absolute continuity identifies E(λ)−Q with its integral. For fixed t, t−g is nonincreasing, so the supremum of initial integrals equals its integral over the positive part.

Tonelli gives the inverse-level formula because the set g<s is an initial interval of length Λ(s) for a<s<b. This holds at jumps and flat intervals, and only open interior s levels matter. At t=b, the tail Stieltjes identity gives Q−D_top and excludes a spurious atom at zero.

Testing the affine envelope at each actual point gives L(F)≤Q−D. A finite-parameter optimizer gives equality at its parameter, and the top own-depth mark gives it by the endpoint identity. The measurable nonnegative remainder is retained even for marks never selected by the envelope.

Strict own-root levels follow by testing the accepted homothetic weak level bound at (s+η)^d and letting η decrease to zero, with null fibers contributing zero and the zero positive-part branch trivial. The moment estimate keeps the exact raw ordinary peak and the accepted factor 1/binom(2d,d); the binomial integral was also checked by exact rational expansion.

At the middle integer mark of the odd product, symmetry gives half the total mass for every nonvertical through-cap and pure-base caps keep at least (N+1)/2 fibers. Opposing nonvertical caps bound Q above by M/2 at every mark. The same mark has maximal own root, so E is affine and the charge is identically zero even though each fiber is strictly lighter than M/2.

dependencies.hypotheses: Same original compact mixed source, summed d-volume, closed ambient raw depth and own-root penalty. Its finite-fiber continuity, right-continuous largest active slope, limit at b and Stieltjes work identity give all the inputs to the conjugate argument.
Each positive fiber is a compact full-dimensional ordinary d-body. Its exact peak A_z is the predecessor's A, so its weak homothetic levels and moment bound apply without changing the measure.

Set m=V_z in the metronoid theorem for a positive fiber; then f=1 almost everywhere is the only admissible density, so the metronoid is the actual centroid and every containing cap there pays Γ_d V_z.

overlap.comparison: The accepted theorem gives the exact scalar envelope, slope and selected-intercept work identity. The frozen proof integrates over every original point and separates the conjugate charge from the deficit remainder.
The accepted level and moment estimates concern ordinary depth on a single fiber. The new budget weights their strict-level sum by the inverse slope of the original mixed envelope.
